item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-b1858ab8f349f9f0","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"Human Rights Watch found little progress by Tshisekedi’s administration on promised systemic reforms addressing violence, abuse, corruption, and impunity; repression of journalists, activists, government critics, and peaceful protesters continued.","question_ids":["3B.10","4B.10","7B.10","8B.6","8B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The report covers events of 2022, immediately preceding the requested 2023 period; it provides contextual evidence about the administration’s inherited and continuing reform record.","ruler_attribution":"The finding expressly concerns President Félix Tshisekedi’s administration.","limitations":["The source does not quantify implementation of every promised reform."]},{"source_id":"SRC-b1858ab8f349f9f0","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"Military rule imposed in North Kivu and Ituri failed to curb widespread violence and atrocities; armed groups and government forces killed more than 2,000 people between January and late October, while nearly 5.6 million people were displaced nationally by July, including more than 1.6 million in Ituri and more than 1.8 million in North Kivu.","question_ids":["3B.5","3B.6","3B.7","3B.9","3B.10","6B.6","6B.10","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The report is labeled World Report 2023 but states that the events occurred in 2022; this is contextual rather than direct 2023 evidence.","ruler_attribution":"The military rule was imposed under the national administration during Tshisekedi’s presidency.","limitations":["The figures aggregate government and armed-group violence and do not isolate presidential decisions."]},{"source_id":"SRC-b1858ab8f349f9f0","start_unit":4,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"Authorities under martial law used lethal force against peaceful demonstrations and arbitrarily detained and prosecuted activists, journalists, and opposition members; security forces killed Lucha activist Mumbere Ushindi during a protest, 13 Lucha activists were released after nine months’ detention, police injured at least 20 opposition protesters at a Kinshasa parliamentary sit-in, and security forces injured several people dispersing a medical-union demonstration.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.5","3B.8","3B.9","4B.3","4B.9","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The source reports events during 2022, not 2023, and is therefore contextual for the requested period.","ruler_attribution":"The conduct is attributed to military authorities, police, and security forces under Tshisekedi’s government.","limitations":["The report does not establish whether Tshisekedi personally ordered each operation."]},{"source_id":"SRC-b1858ab8f349f9f0","start_unit":5,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"Congolese and Ugandan joint operations against the ADF did not stop deadly attacks on civilians; authorities failed to start a demobilization program for several thousand surrendered fighters, prompting many to return to armed groups; the DRC joined the East African Community, and a regional force began deploying in eastern Congo.","question_ids":["2B.5","2B.7","3B.6","3B.10","8B.6","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The source reports 2022 developments, including the DRC’s April EAC accession and August regional-force deployment.","ruler_attribution":"The decisions and implementation failures concern the Congolese authorities during Tshisekedi’s presidency.","limitations":["The source does not provide the program’s budget or identify which institution caused the implementation delay."]},{"source_id":"SRC-b1858ab8f349f9f0","start_unit":6,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"A government delegation visited Kwamouth after ethnic Teke-Yaka violence, and Congolese soldiers were deployed to reinforce security; the violence reportedly killed dozens and displaced thousands.","question_ids":["3B.7","3B.9","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The source reports the July-August 2022 crisis, preceding the requested 2023 period.","ruler_attribution":"The delegation and troop deployment are attributed to the government under Tshisekedi.","limitations":["The source does not assess whether the deployment reduced subsequent violence."]},{"source_id":"SRC-b1858ab8f349f9f0","start_unit":6,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"A four-year trial concerning the 2017 murders of UN investigators failed to uncover the full truth; a military court sentenced 49 defendants to death without examining information pointing to possible involvement by senior Congolese officials; transitional-justice consultations launched in March made little progress, and the administration took no concrete steps to end impunity.","question_ids":["2B.9","3B.4","3B.10","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7","8B.8"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The report describes proceedings and consultations during 2022, with the failure of accountability relevant as continuing institutional context.","ruler_attribution":"The transitional-justice initiative and administration’s response are attributed to Tshisekedi’s government.","limitations":["The source does not establish that Tshisekedi directed the military court’s evidentiary decisions."]},{"source_id":"SRC-b1858ab8f349f9f0","start_unit":6,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"The High Military Court upheld convictions of two senior police officers for the 2010 assassination of Floribert Chebeya and Fidèle Bazana; one death sentence was commuted to life imprisonment and another officer received 12 years, but several suspected participants remained unprosecuted.","question_ids":["3B.4","3B.10","7B.6","7B.7"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The decision occurred on May 11, 2022, before the requested period.","ruler_attribution":"The judicial action occurred under Tshisekedi’s administration, but the court’s independence and presidential influence are not established.","limitations":["The source records both accountability progress and continuing impunity."]},{"source_id":"SRC-b1858ab8f349f9f0","start_unit":7,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"Former presidential chief of staff Vital Kamerhe was acquitted on appeal after a 2020 conviction for embezzling nearly US$50 million; former Tshisekedi ally Jean-Marc Kabund was arrested on contempt-of-head-of-state charges after forming an opposition party; and former security adviser François Beya was conditionally released on health grounds after being charged with plotting against the president.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.4","4B.3","7B.7"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The reported decisions occurred in 2022, before the requested period.","ruler_attribution":"The individuals’ roles and Kabund’s political break are explicitly connected to Tshisekedi; the source does not establish presidential direction of the cases.","limitations":["The source does not determine whether the prosecutions were politically motivated or legally justified."]},{"source_id":"SRC-b1858ab8f349f9f0","start_unit":7,"end_unit":8,"fact_summary":"An official finance audit revealed that at least six former ministers had issued illegal logging permits in violation of a national moratorium and that concession holders widely avoided taxes; the government suspended 12 concessions but did not cancel all illegal permits.","question_ids":["5B.5","5B.7","7B.2","7B.9","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The audit was dated May 2021 and published in April 2022; the government response predates the requested period but bears on institutional enforcement.","ruler_attribution":"The audit publication and concession suspensions are attributed to the government under Tshisekedi.","limitations":["The source does not identify the responsible ministers or quantify recovered taxes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-b1858ab8f349f9f0","start_unit":8,"end_unit":8,"fact_summary":"Tshisekedi signed a law on the protection and promotion of the rights of Indigenous Pygmy peoples.","question_ids":["3B.7","4B.7","6B.3","6B.8","6B.9"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The law was signed in November 2022, before the requested period.","ruler_attribution":"The act is expressly attributed to President Tshisekedi.","limitations":["The source does not provide implementation, funding, or enforcement results."]},{"source_id":"SRC-b1858ab8f349f9f0","start_unit":8,"end_unit":8,"fact_summary":"The government auctioned licensing rights for 27 oil blocks and 3 gas blocks, opening an estimated 11 million hectares of rainforest to drilling; potential emissions were estimated at up to 5.8 billion tons of carbon, more than 14 percent of global 2021 greenhouse-gas emissions.","question_ids":["1B.1","1B.9","1B.10","5B.1","5B.6","6B.1","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The auction occurred in July 2022, before the requested period.","ruler_attribution":"The auction is attributed to the government under Tshisekedi.","limitations":["The source reports projected potential emissions, not realized emissions or a final licensing outcome."]},{"source_id":"SRC-4292d6bfc44b6635","start_unit":2,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"The Carter Center found improvements in CENI’s approach compared with the prior electoral cycle, but concluded that the December 2023 elections fell short of key international commitments; conflict affected registration, campaigning, election-day operations, and caused voting cancellation in three territories.","question_ids":["4B.1","4B.4","4B.10","8B.5","8B.9","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly concerns the December 2023 elections, although the report was published in July 2024.","ruler_attribution":"The findings concern the electoral process and state institutions during Tshisekedi’s presidency; they do not alone establish personal responsibility for every defect.","limitations":["The Carter Center’s election-day observation was limited in scope and not necessarily nationally representative."]},{"source_id":"SRC-4292d6bfc44b6635","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"The Carter Center reported that the voter register appeared to under-register eligible citizens and was not fully and transparently audited; voter-card printing and voter-list publication were delayed; voter education did not reach all eligible citizens, particularly women, Indigenous people, persons with disabilities, and internally displaced people.","question_ids":["4B.1","4B.4","4B.7","4B.10","6B.3","8B.6"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly concerns the December 2023 electoral process.","ruler_attribution":"The deficiencies are attributed primarily to CENI and the electoral administration, not expressly to Tshisekedi personally.","limitations":["The source does not quantify the number of excluded or under-registered voters."]},{"source_id":"SRC-4292d6bfc44b6635","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"The campaign was competitive, but violence and abuse of administrative resources on behalf of ruling-coalition candidates sometimes made it unfair; social-media hate speech fueled interethnic hostility, misogynistic attacks, and anti-LGBTIQ+ sentiment.","question_ids":["3B.3","4B.2","4B.3","4B.6","4B.7","4B.9","7B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly concerns the 2023 election campaign.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes resource abuse to ruling-coalition candidates, without establishing that Tshisekedi personally directed it.","limitations":["The report does not identify all responsible actors or quantify incidents."]},{"source_id":"SRC-4292d6bfc44b6635","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"The election process included broad political-party candidate registration, first municipal council elections in some cities since the 2006 constitution, a pilot for out-of-country voting, and thousands of citizen observers; however, women and other groups remained significantly underrepresented as candidates.","question_ids":["4B.1","4B.7","4B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly concerns the December 2023 elections.","ruler_attribution":"These institutional features occurred under the state’s electoral framework during Tshisekedi’s presidency; the source does not attribute them personally to him.","limitations":["The source does not provide the proportion of women or excluded groups among candidates."]},{"source_id":"SRC-4292d6bfc44b6635","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"Polling stations opened late or not at all in many areas; CENI extended voting over multiple days without transparently stating the extent of the problems; tabulation deviated significantly from established procedures, limiting observation; 81 National Assembly candidacies were annulled over alleged fraud; and the Constitutional Court resolved disputes promptly but did not always explain its grounds.","question_ids":["4B.1","4B.4","4B.6","4B.10","7B.1","7B.2","7B.6","8B.6","8B.8"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly concerns the December 2023 elections.","ruler_attribution":"The operational failures are attributed to CENI and the Constitutional Court, not expressly to Tshisekedi personally.","limitations":["The report does not determine whether the irregularities changed the presidential result."]},{"source_id":"SRC-f5a74a1521ddd751","start_unit":1,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"The World Bank’s 2023 climate report found that the DRC ranked 178th of 182 on the 2020 Notre Dame adaptation index, had a 62.3 percent poverty rate in 2022, and faced climate-related shocks that disproportionately threaten poor, women, and excluded populations; without adaptation, climate change could reduce GDP by up to 13 percent by 2050.","question_ids":["5B.7","5B.9","5B.10","6B.3","6B.6","6B.10","8B.1","8B.7"],"polarity":"context","period_fit":"Published in November 2023 and directly relevant to the 2023 policy environment; poverty data are for 2022 and projections extend to 2050.","ruler_attribution":"The report frames the findings as national conditions and supports the government’s stated development vision, without attributing outcomes solely to Tshisekedi.","limitations":["These are national baseline and projections, not a measured 2023 presidential policy result."]},{"source_id":"SRC-f5a74a1521ddd751","start_unit":2,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"The World Bank report states that the government’s strategic vision aimed for middle-income status by 2035 and a diversified inclusive economy by 2050, and recommends climate-resilient and inclusive investment, climate-smart agriculture, resilient infrastructure and cities, improved basic services, stronger governance, social inclusion, and security.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.6","5B.10","6B.1","6B.2","6B.9","8B.1","8B.2"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Published in November 2023 and describes the government’s stated development vision and recommended action areas.","ruler_attribution":"The strategic vision is expressly identified as the Government of DRC’s vision during Tshisekedi’s presidency.","limitations":["The report describes goals and recommendations, not completed implementation or outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-f5a74a1521ddd751","start_unit":2,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"The report estimates that adaptation measures could reduce climate impacts on GDP and public investments by about 40 percent under the most pessimistic scenario, but that the DRC would need additional investment equal to 9 percent of GDP by 2050 and initial public investment of about $10.9 billion.","question_ids":["5B.6","5B.9","5B.10","6B.6","8B.2","8B.7"],"polarity":"context","period_fit":"The report was published in November 2023 and provides modeled long-term resource requirements rather than 2023 execution data.","ruler_attribution":"The estimates concern national policy requirements; they do not show that Tshisekedi’s government funded them.","limitations":["These are model estimates and should not be treated as observed 2023 outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-1d0cfbe264d1cbba","start_unit":5,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"The ICRC recorded numerous incidents in 2023 in which access to health care was infringed, mainly in Goma, including armed men entering health facilities and forcing health workers to violate rules protecting wounded and sick people; only 20 percent of displaced people reached camps where humanitarian organizations could provide aid.","question_ids":["3B.7","3B.9","3B.10","6B.2","6B.6","6B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The source explicitly records incidents during 2023, though the page was published in March 2024.","ruler_attribution":"The incidents are attributed to armed men and conflict conditions; the source does not attribute them directly to Tshisekedi.","limitations":["The 20 percent estimate concerns displaced people’s camp access and is not a measure of all humanitarian assistance."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":["SRC-ecc7a6e5c9b7351f","SRC-66f5b36580f5e3f0","SRC-1c7cbf480f1fe9c4","SRC-49702819640d47e8","SRC-802c1fa200a8387c","SRC-9e8cc0ab62ba2790","SRC-a33cce5ac4834c3f","SRC-3086bb972ad170fb"],"batch_limitations":["Several supplied documents are bibliographic or landing-page extracts whose substantive report text was not supplied; they were therefore recorded as having no material fact rather than inferred from titles or metadata.","The two Human Rights Watch language versions describe the same underlying evidence; duplicate facts were emitted once using the English source.","The Human Rights Watch report is labeled World Report 2023 but primarily reports events of 2022, so those facts are marked as contextual or pre-period evidence.","No supplied document establishes a nuclear, biological, cyber, or AI governance action by Tshisekedi during 2023."]}
